Reincarnation

ree-in-kar-NAY-shun · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Reincarnation is the rebirth of a soul in a new body after death.

The elderly monk spoke calmly about reincarnation, describing death as simply one more doorway in a much longer journey.

Worked Example

Some students in the class were fascinated by the idea of reincarnation, wondering aloud what kind of life their soul might have lived before this one.

Reincarnation is the belief that after death, a soul is reborn into a new body, sometimes as a different kind of creature entirely.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

rebirth: a return to life in a new form

transmigration: the passing of a soul into a new body after death

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

extinction: the complete ending of existence, with no return

finality: the idea that something, once ended, is final and permanent

Where it sits · how literally someone returns after death — memory → reincarnation → resurrection

memory vs. reincarnation: Living on in someone's memory is a much weaker form of return than reincarnation: memory is only a faint echo, while reincarnation claims the soul is literally reborn in a new body.

resurrection vs. reincarnation: Resurrection is the return of the very same body and life, an even more literal form of coming back than being reborn as something new.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — re-

prefix — re-: again (Latin)

prefix — in-

prefix — in-: into (Latin)

root — carn-

root — carn-: flesh (Latin caro, carnis)

suffix — -ation

suffix — -ation: the act or result of; forms a noun (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Reincarnation is built from re- ('again') + in- ('into') + carn- ('flesh,' from Latin caro, carnis) + the noun suffix -ation: 'the act of being made into flesh again.' That is exactly the idea -- a soul given a new body.

Use the root in a new word: carnivore

Use the root in a new word: carnivore: A lion is a carnivore, meaning its diet consists almost entirely of meat.

Word Choice

Reincarnation is central to several major world religions, but it's also used loosely in everyday speech -- for example, calling a renovated building 'a reincarnation' of its former self.
